top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, mature invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, roughly 1e-18 uncertainty, reproduced and compared across independent laboratories) with a two-name allocation, Katori and Ye, that divides naturally between concept and performance. I regard the Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state as the larger conceptual advance and would weigh it higher on science alone, but the HgTe observation was guided by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, Zhang died in 2018, and no three-name list can repair that omission. That credit defect, which I conceded in round 2, outweighs my weighting of consequence, so P001 goes first. P002 is second, ahead of no award, since the science is sound and mature.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my work in electronic-structure theory and magnetism is adjacent to topological materials, but no documented personal or institutional link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori or Ye
